en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake that surrounds Volcano Island, which itself contains a smaller crater lake.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River, located in the Cagayan Valley region, is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, containing the national capital region of Metro Manila.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for night hunting.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine coral atolls.
The Philippine Sea borders the eastern side of the archipelago and contains the Philippine Trench, one of the deepest oceanic trenches.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
